title: FlutterFlow Pricing 2026: What Every Plan Costs
summary: FlutterFlow pricing is per-seat: $0 Free, $39/month Basic, $80/month Growth. Choose your plan based on export and deployment needs, not app size.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Is FlutterFlow free to use? Yes for building and testing, but the free tier stops short of the two gates that matter: exporting code and deploying a finished app.


You can prototype for a client at no cost, so price the first invoice as if the paid plan already exists.


### Can I cancel or downgrade FlutterFlow at any time?


Yes, it's a subscription, and you can move to a lower plan or leave. The catch is what you lose on the way down: if the plan you drop to doesn't include code export or deployment, those stop working.


Export a copy of the code before downgrading, and confirm the client's app isn't still being served through a plan you're about to shrink.


### Do I own the code FlutterFlow generates?


On a plan that includes code export, you can take the generated code and run it without FlutterFlow. Once you edit that copy by hand, it no longer syncs cleanly with the visual project, so decide early which one is the source of truth.


Whoever holds the account holds the project, so put it in the client's name or write the handover into the contract.


### Does FlutterFlow charge per app user?


No, the subscription is priced per builder seat and plan, not per person who installs your app. Users still cost you money, but the charge lands on the backend: database reads, storage, authentication and any paid services behind the screens.


When an app is a hit, the FlutterFlow line stays flat and the others grow, so quote the client a usage-based run cost rather than a fixed one.


Is there a discount for students or education? FlutterFlow has offered education-oriented access, but eligibility and terms change, so check its pricing page before relying on it.


For an agency, assume no discount applies. A student rate attached to one person's account won't cover a client project, and putting client work on it is the kind of quiet cross-subsidy that causes trouble later.
